newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Senate passes oil and gas industry bill.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Senate passes oil and gas industry bill.

text.p: The Argentine Senate gave its approval late Wednesday to a hydrocarbons bill sent to Congress two years ago, designed to provide a clear legal framework for Argentina's expanding oil and gas industry.
The bill must now be sent to the lower house of Congress for debate before becoming law.

Cesar MacKarthy, Peronist senator for the oil-producing province Chubut, applauded the legislation and said Argentina's oil industry, deregulated from 1991, "deserved more modern legislation to accompany its growth."
The bill "brings more balance to the relationship between oil companies and users," he said.
Lobbying up to the last moment by oil and gas companies toned down some elements of the bill, which stresses consumer rights and environmental protection.

The bill sets out a framework for: efficient assignation and rational use of natural resources; defense of competition against attempts at market manipulation and monopoly; defense of the environment; defense of consumer rights; coordination of oil and gas policy with Argentina's trading partners.
The project would also establish an independent industry watchdog, the eight-member Federal Hydrocarbons Authority.

Legislators said oil companies managed to get the authority's powers on reference prices and a clause about strategic fuel reserves toned down to avoid them being obliged to adapt production to emergency reserve requirements.
The opposition Radical Party voted in favor of the project overall, but said it would like to have seen more emphasis on consumer and environment considerations.
"While the initiative is positive, it is not enough," said Radical Senator Juan Melgarejo.
